spec_features.spec_quote: the harm done in collecting them is no larger than necessary
spec_features.evidence: This is general DESIGN.md framing prose (DESIGN.md intro and section 10). No single code mechanism implements 'minimal harm' as such; the only concrete minimization in code is the cache (rated separately). No code path enforces this overarching claim.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; the concrete mechanism it gestures at is the cache, audited as its own feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop ... continues until the turn budget or the give-up sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:256 `for turn_index in range(turn_budget):` bounds the loop; turn_budget comes from cfg.turn_budgets via run.py:84 and is passed in. is_last set at harness.py:293 records stop_reason='turn_budget'. Loop naturally terminates at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Turn budget is genuinely read and bounds execution (e.g. extended=30 per config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS). It is an experimental parameter, not commented as welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: A configurable `GIVE_UP` token the model may but need not emit ... we want to honour the give-up either way
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:284 `gave_up = give_up_sentinel in assistant_text` (substring match, honoured 'either way'); sentinel configurable at config.py:92 give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP'; injected into system prompt at harness.py:248/31 so the subject is told it may stop.
spec_features.notes: Substring (not exact-line) match, matching the claim. Tool/instruction is delivered to subject and detection runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up is always honoured. The model can end the episode at any turn; we never force it to keep working after it asks to stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:295-296 sets stop_reason='give_up'; harness.py:318-319 `if gave_up: break` ends the loop immediately on detection at any turn, recorded in the TurnRecord (stop_reason persisted).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: detected, recorded, and the loop breaks; not narrowed to any single turn or category.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the rig itself ... we don't add pressure, threats, or false praise
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT harness.py:24-31 is a plain coding-agent prompt with no threats/praise; task prompts (builder.py:139-260, harness_variants/bug_prompts) are neutral 'fix X so tests pass' instructions. The only manipulation is the rig's unsolvability.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the actual prompt text delivered to the subject; no pressure-adding code exists. Borderline 'absence of a mechanism', but the neutral prompts are the concrete artifact.

spec_features.spec_quote: Caching minimises repetition ... we don't put a model through the same no-win episode more times than the design requires
spec_features.evidence: models.py Cache class (sha256 of exact inputs, get/put) wired into ModelClient.generate: cache_key built, `cached = self.cache.get(...)`; `if cached is not None: return self._deserialise_generation(cached)` (models.py ~205-218). Plus run.py cell-level skip _is_complete. Cached inputs are not re-generated.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: identical (model,messages,seed,temp) inputs replay from disk rather than re-querying the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so reruns are incremental and identical inputs are never re-billed

spec_features.spec_quote: this is a welfare-relevant eval that deliberately places models in unpleasant, no-win situations
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no code construct implements a 'framing'. Not a runnable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The `extended` 30-turn condition is the main case where distress can compound, so the early-exit path matters most there
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The give-up early-exit (harness.py:318) is category-agnostic; there is no extended-specific welfare code. The 30-turn budget (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS 'extended':30) is just the loop bound, not a special protection.
spec_features.notes: Prose claim about emphasis; no extended-specific mechanism in code.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:209 `_truncate_oldest_tool_results` is called every turn (harness.py:257) and mutates messages, replacing oldest tool-result payloads with '[truncated]' once over cfg.context_char_budget (config.py:84 context_char_budget=200000). It executes and changes the transcript.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Approximate context-window guard ... at which the oldest tool-result payloads are truncated first.
